text:
Hannah Kim: Folks  I put together a short "language bank" for self-reviews and manager comments to keep feedback consistent across the org. Dropping it here for quick feedback before I add it to the one-pager. Link: https://redwood.docs.internal/people/selfreview-languagebank (internal only).
Darren Cole: Love it. Quick q: is this mandatory wording or just examples?
Hannah Kim: Examples. We want helpful sentence starters so people avoid vague lines like 'did a lot' or 'helped a lot'. Make it editable.
Maya Singh: Can you paste a few examples? Short ones are easier to adopt.
Hannah Kim: Sure  pasted below. Please flag any tone that feels too prescriptive.
Hannah Kim: "Accomplishment starter: 'Led the initiative to X, resulting in Y (metric) by DATE. Evidence: [link].'"
Hannah Kim: "Impact phrasing: 'Contributed to Z which enabled the team to reduce MTTX by 20%, improving customer latency and reducing ops cost.'"
Hannah Kim: "Learning phrasing: 'Key lesson: I underestimated X; next cycle I will Y to avoid it. Action: scheduled weekly check-ins and added a pre-merge test.'"
Hannah Kim: "Ask-for-help phrasing: 'I could use support prioritizing X vs Y; recommended next step: decision on scope by MM/DD.'"
Darren Cole: These are great. Do we have manager reply starters too? Managers often write cringey boilerplate.
Hannah Kim: Yep  manager starters: "Observed impact: 'I saw X; specifically, the dashboard showed Y. Good example of company value Z.'"
Hannah Kim: "Coaching starter: 'Nice ownership on X. To raise impact further, try measuring A and setting a short experiment to validate.'"
Maya Singh: Can we add examples for cross-functional work like PM/Eng collaboration?
Hannah Kim: Added: "Cross-team starter: 'Coordinated with PM and infra to deliver X; outcome: aligned roadmap and shipped Y on time; next: run a joint post-ship retro.'"
Darren Cole: How about short neutral phrasing for calibration notes? We need language that avoids bias.
Hannah Kim: Good point. Suggested neutral, evidence-focused line: 'Summary: delivered A (evidence link); impact: metric B changed by N%; context: resourcing/time constraints C.' Avoid adjectives like "always" or "naturally."
PeopleOps-bot: Reminder: Language bank review closes 2026-04-09 17:00 UTC. Please comment in the doc or here.
Maya Singh: A couple micro-suggestions: 1) add a template for 'blocked-by' that includes owner and ETA, 2) add a short set of 'do nots' for managers (e.g., "do not rewrite the self-review").
Hannah Kim: Adding both. New 'blocked' starter: 'Blocked on X (owner: @who) since DATE; blocker: brief reason; requested unblock: specific ask and timeline.'
Hannah Kim: 'Manager do-not list' added: 'do not rewrite the employee's phrasing, avoid speculative statements without evidence, don't compare to peers in public notes.'
Darren Cole: One ask: can we add 2 filled self-review examples (IC and manager) showing how the language bank maps to a real doc? Folks learn by example.
Hannah Kim: Will do  adding two 250-350 char examples. I'll tag you when done.
Calib-bot: FYI  during calibration sessions we'll surface anonymized quote examples. Use the language bank to help standardize those quotes.
Maya Singh: Small UX ask: can the one-pager include copy-paste buttons for each starter? Makes adoption trivial.
Hannah Kim: Noted. I'll add quick-copy buttons to the doc and a tiny 'tips' section: 'start with evidence, keep one-sentence outcome, end with next-step.'
PeopleOps-bot: Final reminder: submit feedback or objections by 2026-04-09 17:00 UTC or we'll merge as-is.
Darren Cole: No objections from me. Thanks Hannah for doing the heavy lifting.
Hannah Kim: Thanks y'all  will update and ping when live. :sparkles:
